title: Falling ball

reference.basis: cartoon paper shape on wall, not confirmed as A4 and not reliably to scale

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text or narration indicates slow motion; motion is continuous animation

subjects.description: small glossy purple spherical ball falling vertically

observation.what_happens: A purple ball falls vertically in front of a gray wall from mid-height to a brown floor. The motion starts already airborne and ends when the ball contacts the floor.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 4159 px/s² over 4 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x drifts steadily while y falls, hits the floor twice and rebounds lower each time, so horizontal speed is nearly constant and vertical motion is gravity-driven with energy loss at impact. Candidates therefore all share gravity plus a floor bounce with restitution and differ only in air resistance (none vs linear vs quadratic) and impact friction to let the held-back bounces decide.

critique.finding: The ball falls straight down under gravity {g} and hits the floor at {y_floor}. It bounces back up keeping {e} of its downward speed.
critique.headline: Falling ball drops freely and bounces off floor
critique.why_it_won: The winner predicts the bounce off the floor while the plain fall model sails straight through it.

headline: Falling ball drops freely and bounces off floor
finding: The ball falls straight down under gravity 9.81 m/s² and hits the floor at -0.85 ± 6.83e-4 m. It bounces back up keeping 0.6 ± 2.66e-4 of its downward speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: Ball falls under gravity and when its center reaches the floor height the vertical velocity reverses with magnitude scaled by restitution e.
